dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: svadehe jagato vāpi sūkṣmasūkṣmatarāṇi ca | tattvāni yāni nilayaṃ dhyātvānte vyajyate parā ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: If one meditates on the principles (tattvas) of one's own body, or of the world, subtle and ever subtler, as dissolving each into its source, then at the end the supreme Goddess (parā) is revealed.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the technique of fusion (vyāpti): the gross elements are contemplated as absorbed into the subtle elements, these into the ego-principle, that into intellect, that into prakṛti and so on until all is reabsorbed in Sadāśiva; then parā devī is revealed and everything appears as her expression. Singh calls this ātmavyāpti and notes a further stage, śivavyāpti, in verse 57 (Door 034).
dharana.instruction: Let solidity dissolve into fluidity, fluidity into warmth, warmth into movement, movement into space, and space into awareness.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 54 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: awareness (school simplification of the subtler principles)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a nested series, each layer dissolving into the subtler one that contains it, ending in open awareness.
geometry.svg_hint: nested circles, outer ones fading as the eye moves inward to a bright centre
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Fold back into the source
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: each layer of experience is folded back into the subtler one it came from. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Move from the most solid to the most subtle, one layer at a time
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Each layer of the body or world dissolving into its subtler source
attention.secondary: What remains when the layers are folded back

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: If one meditates on the principles (tattvas) of one's own body, or of the world, subtle and ever subtler, as dissolving each into its source, then at the end the supreme Goddess (parā) is revealed.
adiyogi.method_summary: Feel the body's solidity and let it dissolve into fluidity; fluidity into warmth; warmth into movement; movement into space; space into awareness. Rest in what remains. (The full classical series of principles is longer; this is a school simplification.)

honesty.disclosure: Door 031 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 31 (verse 54) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 031 is dharana 31, verse 54. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.
School simplification: the five elements plus awareness stand in for the full classical series of thirty-six principles (tattvas) described in Singh's notes.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Go slowly; if dissolving imagery is unsettling, stop at space and feel the floor. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
